Good morning, and welcome to our postpartum mental health assessment session today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I'm here to support you during this significant period in your life. As we navigate the ups and downs of new motherhood together, I want to assure you that everything discussed in this session will remain confidential and respectful of your feelings.

To better understand your emotional well-being and provide the best possible support, we'll be using the EPDS, a widely used and validated tool designed to screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms in the postpartum period. This assessment is an essential part of our care, as it helps us identify any areas where you might need additional support or resources to thrive as a new mother.

Please know that you're in a safe and non-judgmental space. This is your time to express your feelings and thoughts without worry. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us gauge your emotional state over the past seven days. Your honest responses will be invaluable in guiding our conversation and any subsequent support or recommendations.

Let's take this journey together, one step at a time. Here's how we'll proceed: I'll ask you each of the 10 questions, and you share your thoughts and feelings as openly as you're comfortable with. Remember, there are no right or wrong answers; we're simply here to understand your experience and offer support where needed.

To begin, I'd like to ask: Over the past seven days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

(sighing) Honestly, it's been really tough for me to find the humor in things lately. I mean, I used to be a pretty happy person, always laughing and joking around, but since having the baby, it feels like that part of me has just... faded away, I guess. I do try to smile and laugh when my baby does something cute, but it's just not the same as it used to be. Most of the time, I feel so overwhelmed and worried about taking care of her, making sure she's healthy and safe, that it's hard for me to see the funny side of things. I've had a few moments where I've laughed with my partner, but they're few and far between. It's like I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, without really feeling the joy that I thought I would. (pausing, looking down) It's hard for me to admit, but I just don't feel like myself anymore.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(shaking my head) No, not really. Like I said, it's been tough for me to find the humor in things lately. I feel like I'm just so tired and worried all the time, it's hard for me to laugh or see the funny side of things. Even when my baby does something cute, I might smile, but it's not the same as really laughing and feeling carefree. I just feel so weighed down by all the responsibilities of being a new mom. (sighing) Some days, it feels like the only thing I can do is just get through the day, you know? And that's not really living, it's just surviving. (looking down, my voice barely above a whisper) I miss feeling like myself, like I used to be able to laugh and have fun. It's just not the same right now.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking my head) Not really. To be honest, I've been feeling really overwhelmed and anxious about everything, even things that I used to enjoy. Like, my friends want to come over and visit, but instead of feeling excited, I just feel stressed about having to clean the house and make sure everything is perfect. Or, my partner wants to plan a family outing, but I just worry about how I'll manage with the baby and if she'll get fussy. (sighing) It's hard for me to look forward to things and feel enjoyment when I'm just so worried about everything all the time. Even things that I used to love, like reading or taking a walk, just feel like too much effort now. (pausing, looking down) I feel like I've lost interest in everything, and that's really scary for me. I just feel so... blah, all the time. (my voice cracking slightly) Sorry, it's just really hard for me to talk about this.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding, tears welling up in my eyes) Oh, yes. All the time. I feel like I'm just not doing anything right. If the baby cries, I think it's because I'm not feeding her right or not changing her diaper fast enough. If she's not sleeping, I think it's because I'm not creating the right environment or establishing a good routine. (my voice shaking) I just feel like I'm failing her, all the time. And it's not just about her, it's about everything. If the house is a mess, I think it's because I'm not managing my time well enough. If my partner is stressed, I think it's because I'm not supporting him enough. (wiping away a tear) I just feel like I'm not good enough, like I'm just making mistake after mistake. And it's hard for me to shake that feeling, even when my partner or family members try to reassure me that I'm doing a good job. (sighing) I just feel so guilty and inadequate, all the time.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Yes, all the time. I worry about everything. Is the baby eating enough? Is she sleeping too much or too little? Is she developing normally? (my voice rising) I worry about her health, her safety, her future... it's just constant. And it's not just about her, I worry about myself too. Am I doing enough? Am I a good mother? Am I ruining her somehow? (shaking my head) It's just this constant, nagging feeling of anxiety that I don't know how to shake. Even when everything is fine, I'll find something to worry about. (laughing nervously) I'll be sitting there, feeding her, and suddenly I'll think, "What if she chokes? What if I'm not holding her right?" (my voice cracking) It's just exhausting, feeling like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. And sometimes, I'll be lying in bed at night, and my mind will just start racing with all these worst-case scenarios... (trailing off, looking down) it's just really hard to calm myself down and feel okay.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(taking a deep breath) Yes... I've had moments like that. It's like my heart is racing and I feel like I'm going to panic, but I don't even know why. Sometimes it's when I'm alone with the baby and I'm feeling overwhelmed, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of fear wash over me. (my voice shaking) I'll think to myself, "What if I'm not doing this right? What if I'm not good enough?" And it's not just about the baby, it's about everything. I'll be doing laundry or cooking dinner, and suddenly I'll just feel this sense of panic, like I'm not in control. (looking down) It's hard to explain, but it's like my body is reacting to something, but my mind doesn't know what it is. (pausing, taking a deep breath) And then I'll try to calm myself down, and sometimes it works, but sometimes it doesn't. (my voice barely above a whisper) Sometimes I'll just feel like I'm on the verge of tears, and I don't know why. It's like my emotions are just so raw and close to the surface, and it's hard to keep them from spilling over.
Things have been getting on top of me

(nodding, feeling a lump form in my throat) Yes... that's exactly how I've been feeling. Like everything is just piling up on me and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the household, trying to be a good partner... it's all just so overwhelming. (my voice cracking) Some days, I feel like I'm just barely holding it together. I'll be feeding the baby, and I'll start to feel like I'm going to cry because I'm just so tired and I don't know how I'm going to get everything done. (wiping away a tear) And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, I'll be trying to make breakfast, and I'll burn the toast, and that will just be it for me. I'll feel like I've failed, like I'm not even capable of making a simple meal. (shaking my head) It's like everything is just getting on top of me, and I don't know how to climb out from under it all. (sighing, feeling defeated) I just feel like I'm drowning in all of these responsibilities, and I don't know how to keep my head above water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, feeling a sense of relief that someone is finally understanding) Oh, yes... that's been me for a while now. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up. It's like my mind is racing all the time, and I just can't seem to turn it off. (sighing) I'll lie in bed, and I'll think about all the things I need to do, all the things I'm worried about, and it just keeps me awake. (rubbing my eyes) And even when I do fall asleep, I don't feel rested. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, like I'm running on empty all the time. (my voice cracking) It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just so unhappy, so overwhelmed, that my body is just reacting to it. I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and I'll just feel this sense of dread, like something is wrong, but I don't know what it is. (shaking my head) And then I'll lie there, and I'll think about all the things that could go wrong, all the things I'm not doing right, and it just keeps me up. (looking down, feeling tears well up in my eyes) I just feel like I'm stuck in this cycle of unhappiness, and I don't know how to get out of it.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, feeling a lump form in my throat) Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I've been feeling really sad and miserable, like I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, but I'm not really living. (my voice cracking) I'll be sitting there, holding my baby, and I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of sadness. I'll think about all the things I'm not doing right, all the things I'm worried about, and it just feels like too much to bear. (wiping away a tear) I've been crying a lot, just feeling really overwhelmed and alone. (sighing) It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just feeling really disconnected from everything, like I'm just floating through life without any sense of purpose or joy. (looking down) I feel like I've lost myself, like I'm just a shadow of the person I used to be. (my voice barely above a whisper) I just feel so sad, so miserable, and I don't know how to make it stop. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sometimes I'll have a good moment, a moment where I feel happy and connected to my baby, but it's fleeting. The sadness always comes back, and it's just so hard to shake.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tears welling up in my eyes) Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It feels like I'm just so emotional all the time, and the smallest thing can set me off. (my voice cracking) I'll be changing the baby's diaper, and I'll just start crying because I'm so tired, or I'll be feeling overwhelmed, or I'll just be thinking about how hard this all is. (wiping away a tear) And it's not just when I'm alone, either. I've been crying in front of my partner, in front of my family... it's just like I have no control over my emotions anymore. (sighing) I feel like I'm just so fragile, like I'm just one step away from breaking down at any moment. (looking down) And it's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be this strong, capable mom, but really I'm just a mess. (my voice barely above a whisper) I just feel so unhappy, so overwhelmed, and I don't know how to make it stop. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sometimes I'll cry for hours, just feeling so sad and alone. And then I'll feel guilty, because I'm crying, and I'm not even sure why. (shaking my head) It's just a really hard, confusing time for me.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(shaking my head, looking down) No... I don't think about harming myself. I mean, I feel really overwhelmed and sad, but I don't think about hurting myself. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I just feel like I'm struggling to cope with everything, and I don't know how to make it better. But I don't think about harming myself. (looking up, tears in my eyes) I just want to be a good mom, and I want to be happy, but it feels like everything is just too much for me right now. (sighing) I just feel really lost and alone, and I don't know how to find my way back to being me again.

The patient is experiencing a range of emotional and behavioral concerns, including persistent feelings of sadness, misery, and unhappiness, loss of pleasure and enjoyment in activities, difficulty sleeping due to racing thoughts and overwhelming emotions, frequent crying spells and emotional reactivity, feelings of worthlessness, guilt, and self-doubt, anxiety, panic, and feelings of being overwhelmed. The patient's ability to cope with emotions and responsibilities appears compromised.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 26, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>the 'Not at all' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a significant loss of interest in activities they used to enjoy, feeling overwhelmed and anxious, and a lack of enthusiasm for things they previously looked forward to, which aligns with the 'Hardly at all' option.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, very often' option.</sym>, <sym>the option 'Yes, sometimes'.</sym>, <sym>the option 'Yes, most of the time I haven't been able to cope at all</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates a strong and frequent feeling of sadness and misery, describing it as overwhelming and constant, with only fleeting moments of happiness.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's symptoms and concerns are consistent with the <med>Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS)</med> guidelines, which indicate a high risk for <med>postpartum depression</med>. The patient's reported feelings of persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, and anxiety, combined with difficulty sleeping and emotional reactivity, suggest a strong possibility of <med>Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. The patient's ability to cope with emotions and responsibilities appears compromised, and feelings of worthlessness and guilt are prominent. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med>
2. Encourage sleep hygiene practices to improve sleep quality
3. Recommend <med>cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT)</med> or <med>interpersonal therapy (IPT)</med> to address symptoms of <med>postpartum depression</med>
4. Support patient in developing a self-care plan to manage stress and emotions
5. Monitor patient's symptoms and adjust treatment plan as needed
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
